transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-09-07
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (ArchonCloud Head of Partnerships), Ethan Park (ArchonCloud Cloud Solutions Architect), Ravi Singh (ArchonCloud Biz Dev)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood introduction and partnership model overview; ArchonCloud gave background on their GPU-enabled cloud regions and go-to-market for enterprise SI partners; discussed possible integration points (marketplace listing, private VPC peering, dedicated capacity resell), technical compatibility (VPC, SSO, KMS), and a potential pilot to validate latency and cost for inference workloads. Action items and follow-ups agreed.

Transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samantha from Redwood, AE on the partnership team, with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Maya): Hi Sam, thanks, doing well. Maya here. Good to meet you, excited to learn more.
00:13 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Hey, Ravi. Quick logistics okay on our side.
00:16 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Ethan here — I'll be the tech point for infra stuff.
00:20 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Awesome, great. Quick agenda: we wanted to learn about ArchonCloud's partner motion and infra, share how Redwood works with cloud and GPU vendors, and see overlap on pilots, marketplace, and go-to-market. Sound good?
00:32 Speaker 2 (Maya): Yep, perfect. Maybe I'll kick off with a quick background — we run a region-first cloud focused on high-density GPU tenancy, our customers are ML platforms and enterprise AI teams. We also run a partner marketplace and we do co-sells with systems integrators.
00:48 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We're looking to expand our ecosystem for inference partners; want to support hosted endpoints but also enable customers to use their own VPCs via peering and direct connect.
00:58 Speaker 2 (Maya): We heard about Redwood from a mutual customer who used your dedicated offering and liked the cost controls.
01:06 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Love it — thanks for that high level. Diego, do you want to jump in on the runtime/compatibility side?
01:12 Speaker 2 (Diego): Sure. Quick intro: Redwood provides a unified inference runtime — hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private deployments in a customer's VPC. We optimize for batching, KV cache, quantization profiles, and route requests by policy. For partners we usually look at two patterns — 1) marketplace listing where Archon can spin up Redwood-hosted capacity (our hosted API) backed by your GPUs via an OEM or reseller flow, and 2) VPC/private deployment where a customer uses Archon's infra and we ship a private control plane or an on-prem package.
01:38 Speaker 3 (Ethan): When you say private control plane, is that running in our tenancy or yours? How does the networking work?
01:45 Speaker 2 (Diego): Good Q. We offer a couple of options: a customer-managed control plane that runs in their VPC with a lightweight agent + private tunnel back to Redwood for telemetry, or a fully on-premised closed deployment with no egress depending on compliance needs. In partner cases, we can also provide images that Archon hosts. Networking can be VPC peering or private link; we support SNI and mutual TLS.
02:10 Speaker 1 (Samantha): From a go-to-market side, we usually co-sell and share leads; Archon listing in the partner marketplace drives discovery. Pricing models vary — usage-based for hosted, reserved commits for dedicated, and support/license fees for private.
02:24 Speaker 3 (Maya): For enterprise customers we need clear SLAs and audit trails — SOC 2, audit logs, SSO/SAML, KMS integration. Do you have those baked in?
02:32 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes, SOC 2 is standard for Redwood hosted today, we have audit logs and SAML SSO for the console. For KMS, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping on private deployments, and we can integrate with Archon's key services if required.
02:48 Speaker 3 (Ethan): On the GPU side, we run multiple instance types — Ampere A100s and X-series NVxx, and some customers use third-party accelerators. Any hard constraints on supported GPUs or kernel support?
02:57 Speaker 2 (Diego): We test on A100, H100, and recent Ampere variants; kernel selection is mostly model/sequence-length dependent. For uncommon accelerators we'd need a small validation pass — sometimes optimizations or quantized kernels change perf. We typically do a compatibility matrix with partners.
03:16 Speaker 1 (Samantha): What's Archon's typical enterprise funnel and pilot cadence? Timeline expectations?
03:22 Speaker 3 (Maya): For pilots we usually run 4-8 week POCs, objectives are generally latency under Xms for interactive apps, and cost targets for high volume batch inference. We have procurement timelines that can be 4-6 weeks after technical sign-off.
03:36 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Also procurement will want to see data residency and audit. Some customers are EU only.
03:42 Speaker 2 (Diego): Noted. We can provide documentation and region controls; Redwood can pin model versions and route to region-specific pools.
03:50 Speaker 1 (Samantha): On partner commercial models, we support revenue share, reseller, and referral — flexible. We can put together a suggested pilot pricing for Archon customers.
03:59 Speaker 3 (Maya): Great. Technically, what's required to run Redwood in our marketplace? Is there a container or image?
04:06 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes — we have images and Helm charts for private deployments, and a lightweight agent for telemetry. For a managed hosting flow, we can provide an OEM token and API endpoints. We'll need a small onboarding: network rules, IAM roles, and optionally a peering setup.
04:21 Speaker 4 (Ethan): For the telemetry back channel, are you sending PII or request payloads? We're sensitive about exfil.
04:27 Speaker 2 (Diego): Good point. The private control plane option can be configured to not send payloads — just metrics and aggregated telemetry. For full hosted you'd send tokenized usage and truncated logs for billing. We support field-level encryption and can integrate with customer KMS so the raw tokens never leave your environment if you choose.
04:47 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Can I ask about customer archetypes that most benefit from Archon + Redwood? Who do you see as the ideal joint customer?
04:55 Speaker 3 (Maya): Customers who need enterprise-grade inference but want predictable pricing — fintech, healthcare, and media companies. Also ISVs building LLM app layers that prefer to buy integrated stack from marketplace.
05:05 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Good. Diego, any quick perf anecdotes?
05:08 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yeah, one of our retail customers moved to a dedicated Redwood pool and saw 30-40% token cost reduction via smart batching and KV cache on common prefixes. Latency improvements from kernel selection for short prompt workloads as well.
05:22 Speaker 4 (Ethan): How do you handle model variants for fallback — say H100 is offline, do you route to a cheaper GPU and is there a quality/regression play?
05:30 Speaker 2 (Diego): We have smart routing policies: route-by-cost, latency, region, and we support automatic fallback to quantized variants with quality thresholds and monitoring. Redwood Optimize offers profile suggestions and quality regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
05:46 Speaker 3 (Maya): For the pilot, we'd want to validate a) latency in our region, b) cost per token under expected workload, c) integration with our KMS and SSO. Is that doable in a four week POC?
05:57 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Yes, that's the typical POC checklist. Diego, plan?
06:00 Speaker 2 (Diego): We'll aim for a smoke test in week 1, small benchmark runs in week 2-3 to measure p95 latency and token cost, and a final summary in week 4. We'll need a few sample prompts and the infra diagram from Ethan. Also we'll want to test both hosted+OEM and private-deploy flows to compare UX.
06:16 Speaker 4 (Ethan): On the infra diagram — I'll share our VPC layout and subnet ranges. We also have a strict egress policy for some enterprise accounts, so we'll want to test private link.
06:26 Speaker 3 (Ravi): From GTM, we should coordinate a joint press / blog post if the pilot shows good results.
06:31 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Absolutely — we often do a co-marketing plan. We'll put a first draft after the pilot.
06:36 Speaker 2 (Diego): A few technical clarifications: 1) what model families do your customers typically deploy — Llama family, open LLMs, or larger hosted models? 2) do they require streaming responses? 3) embedding use cases?
06:49 Speaker 3 (Maya): Mostly open LLMs and a mix — some customers have private models. Streaming is important for chat/agent UX and embeddings are a major use-case for search and vector dbs.
07:01 Speaker 2 (Diego): Great — Redwood supports streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings and reranking. For private models we support model onboarding; usually it's a small conversion and we generate a performance profile.
07:12 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Let's talk about high-level integration flows for marketplace listing: 1) Archon lists Redwood offering; 2) customers select either hosted or bring-your-own VPC; 3) for hosted you can route usage via Archon resale with tokens; 4) for BYOVPC we provide onboarding docs. We can share templates for marketplace listing.
07:33 Speaker 3 (Maya): Would we be able to surface performance profiles in our console? e.g., expected p95, throughput, recommended instance types?
07:40 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yes. We can produce a curated profile per model variant and you can ingest that into your marketplace metadata. We also can export benchmark CSVs.
07:49 Speaker 4 (Ethan): On observability, what does tracing look like? Do you provide token-level cost and latency breakdown?
07:55 Speaker 2 (Diego): Yep — Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We can also ship tracing payloads into your existing observability system via OTLP.
08:07 Speaker 3 (Maya): Procurement will ask about termination rights, data deletion, and encryption in transit and at rest. Any red flags?
08:14 Speaker 1 (Samantha): No major red flags. For hosted we retain logs for billing and troubleshooting — retention is configurable and we can provide contract language for deletion. For private deployments, data never leaves the VPC unless you opt into telemetry.
08:26 Speaker 4 (Ethan): For billing/reseller flow, how does metering work if we're doing OEM tokens? Do we get a monthly invoice for consumed tokens on our customers?
08:33 Speaker 1 (Samantha): We support reseller metering where Archon receives consolidated invoices and a detailed usage file. We can also do direct billing if preferred. We'll share sample invoicing formats.
08:44 Speaker 2 (Diego): A couple of technical unknowns for us to validate with Archon: support for your private link implementation and if you have hardware-level isolation for customers on same GPU pools.
08:55 Speaker 3 (Maya): Yes, we can provide dedicated node pools and we do hardware isolation primitives — I'll have Ethan share the exact spec.
09:02 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Perfect. A few quick follow-ups then: we'll send the partner integration doc, a sample Pilot SOW, and suggested pricing. Diego will own the benchmark plan. Maya will share infra details and procurement constraints.
09:14 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Sounds good. One more question — do you have reference customers in finance or healthcare we can show to our sales?
09:21 Speaker 1 (Samantha): We do, won't name names here, but we'll send sanitized reference notes and a short case study of a retail customer and a healthcare pilot with redaction.
09:31 Speaker 2 (Diego): Also we can share a short runbook for on-call and escalation for pilot phase.
09:37 Speaker 3 (Maya): Great. Any technical blockers you foresee?
09:40 Speaker 2 (Diego): Not blockers, just a small compatibility pass for special accelerator types. And we need tenant-level network setup.
09:49 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Okay wrapping up — next steps recap: Samantha to share docs and pricing by 9/10, Ethan to share infra by 9/9, Diego to schedule a deep dive and prep benchmarks for week of 9/21. We'll plan a 30-60 minute technical deep dive.
09:59 Speaker 4 (Ethan): I'll send the VPC diagram and instance details after this call.
10:02 Speaker 3 (Ravi): I'll loop in our partnerships ops and legal contact to the thread.
10:06 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Thanks everyone, really excited to explore this. We'll follow up over email.
10:11 Speaker 2 (Diego): Thanks, bye.
10:12 Speaker 3 (Maya): Bye all.
